squad.quote.unclosed: A double quote is left open at: %s — close it, or drop it if it was not meant to quote.
squad.quote.glued: Text is glued to the closing quote of %s — put a space after it.
squad.arg.stray: Unexpected word %s after the value of %s. Put a value of several words in double quotes.
squad.arg.twice: %s was given as a bare word and again with %s — use one or the other.
board.usage.verbs:
Usage: /board [list [col] | show <id> | archive [age]]
       /board create <title> [--description <text>] [--assignee <agent>] [--column <col>]
       /board edit <id> [<new title>] [--title <text>] [--description <text>]
       /board move <id> <col> | assign <id> <agent> | unassign <id> | note <id> <text>
       /board link <id> [<run-id>] [--run <run-id>] [--job <job-id>]
       /board delete <id> [--yes]
Put a value in double quotes to keep a literal --word in it, or after a one-word flag like --assignee.
board.unassign.ok: Card %s is no longer assigned to anyone.
board.delete.preview: This card would be deleted permanently (nothing was removed yet):
complete.board.edit: Change a card's title or description (edit <id>)
complete.board.link: Link an agent run or job to a card (link <id>)
complete.board.flag.assignee: Worker agent that owns the card
complete.board.flag.title: New title
mail.usage.verbs:
Usage: /mail [list [n] | history [n] | pending | peek [<agent>]]
       /mail send <agent> [--card <card-id>] <text>
--card right after the agent is the unambiguous form; at the very end it only counts when the card exists.
mail.send.recipient_invalid: %s is not a recipient: the agent name comes first, then --card.
mail.send.ok.card: Message queued for %s (%s) about %s — delivered on its next turn.
mail.history.limit_invalid: Invalid limit %s (use a positive number, e.g. /mail history 50)
mail.peek.title: Queued for %s (%d, oldest first — still queued, not delivered yet):
complete.mail.peek: Read queued messages without delivering them (peek [agent])
complete.mail.flag.card: Board card the message is about
agents.wait.timeout_invalid: Invalid timeout %s (use a duration like 90s, 5m or 1h)
agents.wait.hint: Still running — the prompt is yours. Follow it with /agents transcript %s, check again with /agents wait %s, or hold the prompt until it ends with /agents wait %s --block.
agents.wait.block_unavailable: --block is not available on this surface (no terminal to hold). Current state:
agents.wait.block_busy: --block is not available while a turn is running in this session: holding here would stall it. Current state:
agents.wait.holding: Waiting for %s to finish, for at most %s… Ctrl+C gives the prompt back; the agent keeps running.
agents.wait.stale: Stopped waiting: the process that owns %s no longer reports, so it may have died. Last known state:
agents.wait.detached: Stopped waiting. Agent %s keeps running — check it with /agents wait %s.
agents.wait.timed_out: Waited %s and %s is still running. Current state:
agents.transcript.not_mirrored: Run %s belongs to another process (%s) and has mirrored no activity yet — try again in a moment or use /agents show.
agents.transcript.title: Activity of %s — %s (%d of %d entries, oldest first)
agents.transcript.remote: Mirrored from %s via the hub: at most the newest %d entries.
complete.agents.wait: See where a run stands; --block holds until it ends (wait <id>)
complete.agents.flag.block: Hold the prompt until the run ends (Ctrl+C lets go)
complete.agents.flag.timeout: Stop holding after this long (e.g. 5m; default 30m)
complete.agents.flag.tail: How many entries from the end
